rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph addresses the two prisoners and anyone in Egypt who shares their religion.
rows.anchor: خطاب لهما ولمن على دينهما من أهل مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their gods are only names assigned by them and their fathers, with no proof of divinity; they worship labels rather than real divine beings.
rows.anchor: إلا أشياء باعتبار أسام أطلقتم عليها من غير حجة تدل على تحقق مسمياتها فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment concerning worship belongs only to God, inherently worthy of worship as necessary in being, creator of all, and owner of all affairs.
rows.anchor: لأنه المستحق لها بالذات من حيث إنه الواجب لذاته الموجد للكل والمالك لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded through His prophets that worship be directed only to Him, as the proofs establish.
rows.anchor: على لسان أنبيائه. { ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه } الذي دلت عليه الحجج.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upright religion is truth; the passage advances the call gradually, first arguing rhetorically for monotheism, then disproving the idols' divinity, then stating the rationally sound faith; most people remain ignorant.
rows.anchor: وهذا من التدرج في الدعوة وإلزام الحجة، بين لهم أولا رجحان التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the dream confused false dreams; ḍighth originally means a bundle of mixed plants and was borrowed for a false dream.
rows.anchor: أضغاث أحلام وهي تخاليطها جمع ضغث وأصله ما جمع من أخلاط النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural may exaggerate how utterly false the dream is, as in saying someone rides horses, or indicate that it contains diverse things.
rows.anchor: وإنما جمعوا للمبالغة في وصف الحلم بالبطلان كقولهم: فلان يركب الخيل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean specifically false dreams, which they say have no interpretation; this is a second excuse, since only true dreams are interpreted.
rows.anchor: يريدون بالأحلام المنامات الباطلة خاصة أي ليس لها تأويل عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer calls Joseph exceptionally truthful because he experienced the accurate interpretation of his own dream and his companion's.
rows.anchor: وإنما وصفه بالصديق وهو المبالغ في الصدق لأنه جرب أحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks Joseph to interpret the king's dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones and green and dry ears of grain.
rows.anchor: أي في رؤيا ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people he hopes to return to may be the king and his court, or the townspeople if the prison was outside the city.
rows.anchor: أعود إلى الملك ومن عنده، أو إلى أهل البلد إذا قيل إن السجن لم يكن فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may learn the dream's interpretation or Joseph's excellence and standing; he speaks tentatively because he may not return alive.
rows.anchor: تأويلها أو فضلك ومكانك، وإنما لم يبت الكلام فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying he does not absolve himself avoids self-praise and instead acknowledges God's gift of protection and success.
rows.anchor: لا أنزهها تنبيها على أنه لم يرد بذلك تزكية نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Joseph said he had not betrayed the absent master, Gabriel asked whether this was so even when he had intended it; Joseph affirmed it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه لما قال: { ليعلم أنى لم أخنه بالغيب } قال له جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul persistently urges evil because its nature inclines toward desires and makes the faculties and limbs pursue them.
rows.anchor: من حيث إنها بالطبع مائلة إلى الشهوات فتهم بها، وتستعمل القوى والجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may mean the times when God shows mercy, or the souls He protects from evil.
rows.anchor: إلا وقت رحمة ربي، أو إلا ما رحمه الله من النفوس فعصمه من ذلك.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception is disconnected: only God's mercy turns away wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وقيل الاستثناء منقطع أي ولكن رحمة ربي هي التي تصرف الإساءة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, this is the wife of al-Aziz speaking, with Joseph and those like him excepted from the soul's urging.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية حكاية قول راعيل والمستثنى نفس يوسف وأضرابه.

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
rows.claim: They read al-sūʾ with the hamza changed into wāw and then assimilated.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن كثير ونافع { بالسو } على قلب الهمزة واوا ثم الادغام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives the soul's impulses and shows mercy through protection, or forgives and has mercy on a sinner who confesses and seeks forgiveness.
rows.anchor: يغفر هم النفس ويرحم من يشاء بالعصمة أو يغفر للمستغفر لذنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king wants Joseph brought to make him his own trusted adviser; after speaking with him and seeing his discernment, he calls him established and trustworthy.
rows.anchor: أجعله خالصا لنفسي. { فلما كلمه } أي فلما أتوا به فكلمه وشاهد منه الرشد والدهاء.

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: After leaving prison Joseph bathed, dressed in new clothes, prayed for protection from the king's evil and for his good, greeted him in Hebrew, and explained it was his fathers' language; the king knew seventy languages and Joseph answered him in them all.
rows.anchor: اغتسل وتنظف ولبس ثيابا جددا، فلما دخل على الملك

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: The amazed king asked Joseph to recount his dream; Joseph described the cows and ears as seen, and the king seated him on the throne and entrusted him with authority.
rows.anchor: أحب أن أسمع رؤياي منك، فحكاها ونعت له البقرات والسنابل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Qitfir died during those nights; Joseph took his post, married Ra'il, found her a virgin, and had Ephraim and Misha by her.
rows.anchor: وقيل توفي قطفير في تلك الليالي فنصبه منصبه وزوج منه راعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to govern Egypt's storehouses, promising to guard them from the undeserving and to know how to manage them.
rows.anchor: ولني أمرها والأرض أرض مصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the king would use him in any case, Joseph chose an office whose benefits would be broad and great.
rows.anchor: لما رأى أنه يستعمله في أمره لا محالة آثر ما تعم فوائده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage supports seeking appointment, declaring one's competence, and serving under an unbelieving ruler when that is the only way to uphold justice and govern people.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على جواز طلب التولية وإظهار أنه مستعد لها والتولي من يد الكافر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that the king accepted Islam at Joseph's hand.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أن الملك أسلم على يده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God established Joseph in Egypt, where he could settle wherever he wished; His mercy reaches whom He wills in this life and the next, and He fully rewards those who do good now and later.
rows.anchor: في أرض مصر. { يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء } ينزل من بلادها حيث يهوى

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads 'we wish' with the nūn rather than the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «نشاء» بالنون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife's reward is better because it is great and lasting, for those who believe and avoid associationism and sexual immorality.
rows.anchor: خير للذين ءامنوا وكانوا يتقون } الشرك والفواحش لعظمه ودوامه.

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: As vizier, Joseph administered justice, increased cultivation, and controlled harvests; when famine struck Egypt, Syria, and surrounding lands, he sold provisions first for money, then valuables, livestock, estates, and finally the people themselves.
rows.anchor: لما استوزره الملك أقام العدل واجتهد في تكثير الزراعات وضبط الغلات، حتى دخلت السنون المجدبة

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: Joseph then consulted the king, who left the decision to him; Joseph freed the people and returned their property, while Jacob sent all his sons except Benjamin for provisions.
rows.anchor: فقال: الرأي رأيك فأعتقهم ورد عليهم أموالهم، وكان قد أصاب كنعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him because time had passed, they had last seen him as a child, thought he had perished, and were awed by his changed status and appearance.
rows.anchor: لطول العهد ومفارقتهم إياه في سن الحداثة ونسيانهم إياه، وتوهمهم أنه هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph fully outfitted them and loaded their camels; jihāz means provisions prepared for travel or transfer, a bride's trousseau, and related equipment.
rows.anchor: أصلحهم بعدتهم وأوقر ركائبهم بما جاؤوا لأجله، والجهاز ما يعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading pronounces jihāz with kasra on the first consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { بجهازهم } بالكسر.

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: Joseph suspected them of espionage; they explained that they were sons of the prophet Jacob, said one brother had perished and another stayed with their father, and could find no local witness.
rows.anchor: قال: من أنتم وما أمركم لعلكم عيون؟ قالوا: معاذ الله إنما نحن بنو أب واحد

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: Joseph required one brother as a hostage while they brought Benjamin; the brothers drew lots and Simeon was selected.
rows.anchor: قال: فدعوا بعضكم عندي رهينة وائتوني بأخيكم من أبيكم حتى أصدقكم، فاقترعوا فأصابت شمعون.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, Joseph gave each man one camel-load, and when they requested an extra load for their half-brother, he granted it on condition that they bring him.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان يوسف يعطي لكل نفر حملا فسألوه حملا زائدا لأخ لهم من أبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says he gives the full measure and is the best host, having treated them generously.
rows.anchor: ألا ترون أني أوفى الكيل } أتمه. { وأنا خير المنزلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they do not bring Benjamin, they will receive no measure and must not approach Joseph or enter his residence.
rows.anchor: أي ولا تقربوني ولا تدخلوا دياري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause may be a prohibition or a negation coordinated with the consequence.
rows.anchor: وهو إما نهي أو نفي معطوف على الجزاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers promise to strive to persuade their father to let Benjamin come and say they will not delay.
rows.anchor: سنجتهد في طلبه من أبيه. { وإنا لفعلون } ذلك لا نتوانى فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fityān means Joseph's measuring servants; Hamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read the intensive plural fityānah to match the one servant assigned to each load.
rows.anchor: لغلمانه الكيالين جمع فتى. وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص«لفتيانه» على أنه جمع الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph returned their payment, sandals and leather, from generosity and dignity, and because their father might lack anything with which to repay it.
rows.anchor: وكانت نعالا وأدما وإنما فعل ذلك توسيعا وتفضلا عليهم وترفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may recognize the returned payment itself or recognize their obligation to return it.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يعرفون حق ردها. أو لكي يعرفوها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they return home and open their containers, recognizing the goods may induce them to come back.
rows.anchor: انصرفوا ورجعوا. { إلى أهلهم } وفتحوا أوعيتهم. { لعلهم يرجعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers say the ruler has barred further grain unless Benjamin comes, and ask their father to send him so they can remove that obstacle and obtain what they need.
rows.anchor: حكم بمنعه بعد هذا إن لم نذهب ببنيامين. { فأرسل معنا أخانا نكتل }

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read the verb with yāʾ, referring to Benjamin: he will measure for himself in addition to their allotments.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالياء على إسناده إلى الأخ أي يكتل لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to protect their brother from harm.
rows.anchor: وإنا له لحفظون } من أن يناله مكروه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob recalls that the brothers previously made the same promise about Joseph.
rows.anchor: وقد قلتم في يوسف: { وإنا له لحفظون }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best protector, so Jacob entrusts the matter to Him; ḥifẓan is parsed as specification, and in the named reading it can be circumstantial.
rows.anchor: فأتوكل عليه وأفوض أمري إليه، وانتصاب «حفظا» على التمييز

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: They read the phrase as 'a better keeper'; other readings include 'better in keeping' and 'the best of keepers.'
rows.anchor: والحال كقوله: لله دره فارسا، وقرىء { خير حفظا } و «خير الحافظين».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob hopes God's protection and mercy will spare him a second bereavement.
rows.anchor: فارجوا أن يرحمني بحفظه ولا يجمع على مصيبتين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading transfers the kasra of the doubled dāl onto the rāʾ in rudd at, as in the cited examples bayʿ and qīl.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { ردت } بنقل كسرة الدال المدغمة إلى الراء نقلها في بيع وقيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'What more could we want?' may mean that the ruler has already honored and hosted them, sold them grain, and returned their payment; alternatively, they seek no further favor or will not embellish their account.
rows.anchor: ماذا نطلب هل من مزيد على ذلك أكرمنا وأحسن مثوانا وباع منا ورد علينا متاعنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading addresses their father: what further kindness or evidence of their truth could he want?
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ما تبغي» على الخطاب أي: أي شيء تطلب وراء هذا من الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'This is our payment returned' explains their claim that they want nothing more.
rows.anchor: هذه بضعتنا ردت إلينا } استئناف موضح لقوله { ما نبغى }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plan to provision the family is coordinated with an omitted clause: they will use the returned payment and go back to the ruler.
rows.anchor: ونمير أهلنا } معطوف على محذوف أي ردت إلينا فنستظهر بها ونمير أهلنا بالرجوع إلى الملك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to protect Benjamin on both legs of the journey and gain his extra camel-load by bringing him.
rows.anchor: ونحفظ أخانا } عن المخاوف في ذهابنا وإيابنا. { ونزداد كيل بعير } وسق بعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'That is a small measure' may mean their allotment is insufficient, or that one camel-load is too little for the ruler to begrudge; alternatively Jacob says one load is too little to risk a son for.
rows.anchor: ذلك كيل يسير } أي مكيل قليل لا يكفينا، استقلوا ما كيل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob refuses because of what happened before and requires a solemn covenant invoking God; the clause is an oath's answer, since they must swear to bring Benjamin.
rows.anchor: إذ رأيت منكم ما رأيت. { حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله } حتى تعطوني ما أتوثق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception allows for being overpowered and unable, or all of them perishing; grammatically it may be from all circumstances or causes, with the oath phrase understood as a negative demand.
rows.anchor: إلا أن تغلبوا فلا تطيقوا ذلك أو إلا أن تهلكوا جميعا وهو استثناء مفرغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their pledge is their covenant, and God is a watchful witness to Jacob's demand and their promise.
rows.anchor: فلما ءاتوه موثقهم } عهدهم. { قال الله على ما نقول } من طلب الموثق وإتيانه. { وكيل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob advised separate entrances because his handsome, impressive sons were known in Egypt for royal favor and honor, and he feared they might be envied or harmed together; perhaps he had not advised this before because they were unknown or because only Benjamin concerned him.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا ذوي جمال وأبهة مشتهرين في مصر بالقربة والكرامة عند الملك، فخاف عليهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic supplication seeks God's protection from every devil, poisonous creature, and harmful evil eye.
rows.anchor: اللهم إني أعوذ بكلمات الله التامة من كل شيطان وهامة ومن كل عين لامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's precautions cannot avert anything God has decreed; caution does not prevent destiny.
rows.anchor: مما قضى عليكم بما أشرت به إليكم فإن الحذر لا يمنع القدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone decides what befalls them, and if harm is decreed their precautions cannot prevent it.
rows.anchor: يصيبكم لا محالة إن قضي عليكم سوء ولا ينفعكم ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated preposed 'upon Him' gives exclusivity; the clauses are coordinated, with faʾ signaling consequence because prophets' conduct should be followed.
rows.anchor: جمع بين الحرفين في عطف الجملة على الجملة لتقدم الصلة للاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers entered by separate gates, but Jacob's advice and their compliance could not avert God's decree; Benjamin was taken after the cup was found and Jacob's loss doubled.
rows.anchor: أي من أبواب متفرقة في البلد. { ما كان يغنى عنهم } رأي يعقوب واتباعهم له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected: Jacob's inner need was his concern for them and caution against the evil eye, fulfilled by giving the advice.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي ولكن حاجة في نفسه، يعني شفقته عليهم وحرازته من أن يعانوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob had knowledge through revelation and proofs, so he did not mistake planning for protection from destiny; most people do not know that caution cannot overcome fate.
rows.anchor: وإنه لذو علم لما علمناه } بالوحي ونصب الحجج، ولذلك قال { وما أغنى عنكم

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: Joseph hosted the brothers in pairs; when Benjamin was left alone he wept, Joseph seated him beside himself, then arranged for them to room in pairs and kept Benjamin with him.
rows.anchor: روي: (أنه أضافهم فأجلسهم مثنى مثنى فبقي بنيامين وحيدا فبكى وقال: لو كان أخي يوسف حيا

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: Benjamin said no brother could match Joseph but that the same parents had not borne Joseph; Joseph wept, embraced him, and revealed his identity.
rows.anchor: قال: من يجد أخا مثلك ولكن لم يلدك يعقوب ولا راحيل، فبكى يوسف وقام إليه وعانقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph tells Benjamin not to grieve over what the brothers had done to them in the past.
rows.anchor: بما كانوا يعملون } في حقنا فيما مضى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sāqiya was a drinking vessel; some say it was a silver measuring cup, others a vessel for watering animals and measuring, and another view says it was gold.
rows.anchor: قيل كانت مشربة جعلت صاعا يكال به وقيل: كانت تسقى الدواب بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has jaʿala with an omitted response to 'when'; the implied continuation is that Joseph let them depart.
rows.anchor: وقرىء و «جعل» على حذف جواب فلما تقديره أمهلهم حتى انطلقوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller may have accused them without Joseph's instruction, or the cup's placement and the call may have been with Benjamin's consent.
rows.anchor: لعله لم يقله بأمر يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام أو كان تعبية السقاية والنداء عليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, 'you are thieves' refers to their earlier taking Joseph from his father; a variant reads the words as a question.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه إنكم لسارقون يوسف من أبيه أو أئنكم لسارقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĪr means a caravan and originally names loaded camels as they travel; the address refers to their owners, as in the prophetic call 'O God's cavalry, ride.' Another account derives it as a collective noun and says it was extended to caravans generally.
rows.anchor: والعير القافلة وهو اسم الإبل التي عليها الأحمال لأنها تعير أي تتردد، فقيل لأصحابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask what has gone missing; faqad means an object's absence from perception when its location is unknown.
rows.anchor: أي شيء ضاع منكم، والفقد غيبة الشيء عن الحس بحيث لا يعرف مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading uses afqadtu, meaning 'you found him missing.'
rows.anchor: وقرىء { تفقدون } من أفقدته إذا وجدته فقيدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings vary between ṣuwāʿ, ṣāʿ, ṣūʿ, with different vowels and ʿayn or ghayn, and ṣawāgh from metalworking.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «صاع» و «صوع» بالفتح والضم والعين والغين و «صواغ» من الصياغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The finder is promised a camel-load of food; the speaker guarantees payment. This supports reward contracts and guaranteeing a reward before work is complete.
rows.anchor: من الطعام جعلا له. { وأنا به زعيم } كفيل أؤديه إلى من رده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in their oath replaces the bāʾ, is used specifically with God's name, and conveys astonishment.
rows.anchor: قسم فيه معنى التعجب، التاء بدل من الباء مختصة باسم الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They appeal to the officials' knowledge of their honesty, including their returned payment and muzzled animals kept from others' crops and food.
rows.anchor: استشهدوا بعلمهم على براءة أنفسهم لما عرفوا منهم في كرتي مجيئهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for the thief's punishment, the punishment for theft, or the cup's punishment, with a genitive noun omitted; they ask in case the brothers lied about being innocent.
rows.anchor: فما جزاء السارق أو السرق أو ال { صواع } على حذف المضاف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule they propose is to detain and enslave whoever has the stolen property in his baggage; this was Jacob's law.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء سرقته أخذ من وجد في رحله واسترقاقه، هكذا كان شرع يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'He is its penalty' may restate the ruling or serve as the predicate of man; the faʾ reflects conditional meaning or marks a conditional answer, and the whole sentence stands as predicate of the penalty.
rows.anchor: تقرير للحكم وإلزام له، أو خبر { من } والفاء لتضمنها معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say that is how wrongdoers are punished for theft.
rows.anchor: كذلك نجزى الظلمين } بالسرقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller began searching the brothers' baggage; another view says Joseph began, since they had returned to Egypt.
rows.anchor: فبدأ المؤذن. وقيل يوسف لأنهم ردوا إلى مصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Searching Benjamin's brothers first removed suspicion; the extracted item may be the sāqiya or ṣuwāʿ, since the noun can be masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: بنيامين نفيا للتهمة. { ثم استخرجها } أي السقاية أو الصواع لأنه يذكر ويؤنث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading rounds the wāw or changes it to hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بضم الواو وبقلبها همزة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God devised this plan for Joseph by teaching and revealing it to him.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الكيد. { كدنا ليوسف } بأن علمناه إياه وأوحينا به إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptian law punished theft by beating and repayment of twice the value, not enslavement; this explains why Joseph could not otherwise keep his brother under the king's law.
rows.anchor: ملك مصر لأن دينه الضرب وتغريم ضعف ما أخذ دون الاسترقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may mean God made the king's rule conform to this case; alternatively it is disconnected, since Joseph could take his brother only by God's will and permission.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل ذلك الحكم حكم الملك، فالاستثناء من أعم الأحوال ويجوز أن يكون منقطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raises whom He wills by knowledge; above each learned person is one more learned.
rows.anchor: نرفع درجات من نشاء } بالعلم كما رفعنا درجته. { وفوق كل ذي علم عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse has been used to argue that God is knowledgeable through His essence, since otherwise something would stand above Him in knowledge.
rows.anchor: واحتج به من زعم أنه تعالى عالم بذاته إذ لو كان ذا علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument fails because the statement concerns created people; al-ʿalīm is God, whose knowledge is complete, as in saying a knower stands above all scholars.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن المراد كل ذي علم من الخلق لأن الكلام فيهم ولأن العليم هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers say that if Benjamin stole, his brother Joseph had stolen before him.
rows.anchor: بنيامين. { فقد سرق أخ له من قبل } يعنون يوسف.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One story says Joseph's aunt inherited Abraham's belt, kept Joseph after he tied it around himself, then claimed it missing, making him hers by their law.
rows.anchor: قيل ورثت عمته من أبيها منطقة إبراهيم عليه السلام وكانت تحضن يوسف وتحبه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another story says Joseph stole and smashed his maternal grandfather's idol, casting it among dung.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان لأبي أمه صنم فسرقه وكسره وألقاه في الجيف.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Joseph gave a beggar a young animal or a chicken that was in the house.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان في البيت عناق أو دجاجة فأعطاها السائل.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Joseph entered a church and took a small golden statue.
rows.anchor: وقيل دخل كنيسة وأخذ تمثالا صغيرا من الذهب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'Joseph hid it' may refer to his answer, their statement, or their attribution of theft to him.
rows.anchor: أكنها ولم يظهرها لهم، والضمير للإجابة أو المقالة أو نسبة السرقة إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun is cataphoric, explained by 'you are worse in standing,' as if Joseph thought they were worse thieves for stealing their brother or worse in conduct; its feminine form refers to a word or sentence.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها كناية بشريطة التفسير يفسرها قوله: { قال أنتم شر مكانا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cataphoric analysis is problematic because a whole explanatory sentence can only explain the pronoun of the matter.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر إذ المفسر بالجملة لا يكون إلا ضمير الشأن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows that their accusation is false.
rows.anchor: وهو يعلم أن الأمر ليس كما تصفون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob is a great elder either because of age or standing; the brothers mention his condition to arouse Joseph's compassion.
rows.anchor: أي في السن أو القدر، ذكروا له حاله استعطافا له عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They offer to leave one of themselves in Benjamin's place because their father, bereaved of the son believed dead, is comforted by Benjamin.
rows.anchor: بدله فإن أباه ثكلان على أخيه الهالك مستأنس به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may mean Joseph has already treated them kindly and should complete his kindness, or that he is known for a habit of kindness he should maintain.
rows.anchor: إلينا فأتمم إحسانك، أو من المتعودين بالإحسان فلا تغير عاداتك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph refuses to take anyone but the person whose baggage contains the cup, since taking another would violate the brothers' own proposed rule; God permitted taking the finder for his benefit and consent.
rows.anchor: فإن أخذ غيره ظلم على فتواكم فلو أخذنا أحدكم مكانه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers lose hope in Joseph's agreement; the added sīn and tāʾ intensify the verb.
rows.anchor: يئسوا من يوسف وإجابته إياهم، وزيادة السين والتاء للمبالغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They withdrew alone for private counsel; najiyyan is a singular verbal noun or a collective form like ṣadīq, with plural anjiya as in nadī and andiya.
rows.anchor: انفردوا واعتزلوا. { نجيا } متناجين، وإنما وحده لأنه مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eldest may mean Reuben by age or Simeon by judgment; another view names Judah.
rows.anchor: في السن وهو روبيل، أو في الرأي وهو شمعون وقيل يهوذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father's covenant is described as from God because the oath invoked God with His permission and confirmation.
rows.anchor: عهدا وثيقا، وأنما جعل حلفهم بالله موثقا منه لأنه بإذن منه وتأكيد من جهته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'What you neglected regarding Joseph' means you fell short in his affair; mā may be extra or a verbal noun, with several possible grammatical attachments and parses.
rows.anchor: قصرتم في شأنه، و { ما } مزيدة ويجوز أن تكون مصدرية في موضع النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will stay in Egypt until his father permits his return or God decrees his departure, Benjamin's release, or a fight to free him.
rows.anchor: فلن أفارق أرض مصر. { حتى يأذن لى أبى } في الرجوع. { أو يحكم الله لى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report, Reuben threatened a cry so loud pregnant women would miscarry; his hair stood out through his clothes, and Joseph sent his son to touch him, calming him. Reuben recognized a descendant of Jacob in the land.
rows.anchor: لأصيحن صيحة تضع منها الحوامل، ووقفت شعور جسده فخرجت من ثيابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best of judges because His judgment is always just.
rows.anchor: لأن حكمه لا يكون إلا بالحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers tell Jacob Benjamin stole according to what they observed; a reading says he was accused of theft.
rows.anchor: على ما شاهدناه من ظاهر الأمر. وقرىء { سرق } أي نسب إلى السرقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They testify only to what they knew: they saw the cup taken from Benjamin's baggage.
rows.anchor: بأن رأينا أن الصواع استخرج من وعائه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were not guardians of the unseen: they did not know whether Benjamin stole or the cup had been placed in his baggage, or they could not know future events such as his theft or their loss of him.
rows.anchor: لباطن الحال. { حفظين } فلا ندري أنه سرق أو سرق الصواع في رحله، أو وما كنا للعواقب عالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town may be Egypt or a nearby settlement where the caller found them; they mean to ask its people about what happened.
rows.anchor: يعنون مصر أو قرية بقربها لحقهم المنادي فيها، والمعنى أرسل إلى أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also appeal to the people traveling with their caravan and reinforce their statement with an oath-like assurance.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب العير التي توجهنا فيهم وكنا معهم. { وإنا لصدقون } تأكيد في محل القسم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says their souls had planned and made the deed seem easy; otherwise, the ruler would not know that a thief is punished by taking the thief.
rows.anchor: أي سولت وسهلت. { لكم أنفسكم أمرا } أردتموه فقدرتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Beautiful patience' may mean that his affair is one of beautiful patience, or that beautiful patience itself is best.
rows.anchor: أي فأمري صبر جميل، أو فصبر جميل أجمل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob hopes God will bring all three sons—Joseph, Benjamin, and the brother remaining in Egypt—back to him.
rows.anchor: بيوسف وبنيامين وأخيهما الذي توقف بمصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows Jacob's and his sons' circumstances and wisely governs their affairs.
rows.anchor: بحالي وحالهم. { الحكيم } في تدبيرهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob turns away from his sons and calls for his sorrow; asaf is intense grief and regret, and its final alif replaces the first-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وأعرض عنهم كراهة لما صادف منهم. { وقال يا أسفا على يوسف } أي يا أسفا تعالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob mourns Joseph more because that first loss set the pattern for later calamities, Joseph was young and dear to his heart, and Jacob trusted the other two were alive while he could not be sure of Joseph.
rows.anchor: لأن رزأه كان قاعدة المصيبات وكان غضا آخذا بمجامع قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says only Muhammad's community, unlike earlier communities, was given the formula 'We belong to God and return to Him' at calamity.
rows.anchor: عند المصيبة إلا أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His eyes whitened from extensive weeping, as tears seemed to erase their blackness; alternative views say his eyesight weakened or he became blind.
rows.anchor: لكثرة بكائه من الحزن كأن العبرة محقت سوادهما. وقيل ضعف بصره. وقيل عمي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has min al-ḥuzn with a different vowel pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { من الحزن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account permits grieving and crying when struck by loss; such reactions may lie beyond ordinary moral control in severe distress.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على جواز التأسف والبكاء عند التفجع، ولعل أمثال ذلك لا تدخل تحت التكليف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet wept for his son Ibrahim, saying the heart grieves and the eyes shed tears, while one says only what pleases the Lord.
rows.anchor: القلب يجزع والعين تدمع، ولا نقول ما يسخط الرب، وإنا عليك يا إبراهيم لمحزونون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaẓīm means Jacob was full of anger toward his sons but kept it in his heart without displaying it; it can be passive ('restrained') or active ('restraining'), with Quranic parallels and the image of a camel holding cud in its stomach.
rows.anchor: مملوء من الغيظ على أولاده ممسك له في قلبه لا يظهره، فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafʾaʾ means 'you do not cease'; lā is omitted because an unmarked oath is understood negatively, as in the cited poetic line.
rows.anchor: أي لا تفتأ ولا تزال تذكره تفجعا عليه، فحذف لا كما في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaraḍ means an illness near death, or someone consumed by grief or sickness; originally a verbal noun, it is not made feminine or plural, and its adjective is read with kasra or ḍamma.
rows.anchor: مريضا مشفيا على الهلاك. وقيل الحرض الذي أذابه هم أو مرض، وهو في الأصل مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read with kasra or with two ḍammas, like janub.
rows.anchor: وقد قرىء به وبضمتين كجنب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They warn that Jacob might become one of the dead.
rows.anchor: من الميتين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's distress is worry he cannot bear to contain, from a root meaning to spread; he complains to God alone, not to his family or anyone else.
rows.anchor: همي الذي لا أقدر الصبر عليه من البث بمعنى النشر. { إلى الله } لا إلى أحد منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He knows from God's actions and mercy that God does not disappoint a supplicant or abandon one who takes refuge in Him, or he knows through inspiration.
rows.anchor: من صنعه ورحمته فإنه لا يخيب داعيه ولا يدع الملتجىء إليه، أو من الله بنوع من الإلهام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What Jacob knows is that Joseph is alive; one report says he asked the Angel of Death in a dream and was told Joseph lived, while another says Joseph's dream showed he would not die before his brothers prostrated to him.
rows.anchor: من حياة يوسف. قيل رأى ملك الموت في المنام فسأله عنه فقال هو حي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob tells his sons to investigate and sense out news of Joseph and Benjamin.
rows.anchor: فتعرفوا منهما وتفحصوا عن حالهما والتحسس تطلب الإحساس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not despair of God's relief and release; a reading understands rūḥ as God's mercy through which living creatures live.
rows.anchor: ولا تقنطوا من فرجه وتنفيسه. وقرىء { من روح الله } أي من رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only disbelievers despair of God's mercy, since a believer who knows God and His attributes does not despair in any circumstance.
rows.anchor: فإن العارف المؤمن لا يقنط من رحمته في شيء من الأحوال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers have returned to Egypt for a second trip; they say severe hunger has afflicted them and their family.
rows.anchor: بعدما رجعوا إلى مصر رجعة ثانية. { مسنا وأهلنا الضر } شدة الجوع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their meager payment may have been poor quality or scant; it was unwanted and pushed away. Reports identify it as counterfeit dirhams, wool and clarified butter, pine nuts and green grain, or dried curds and ground locust beans.
rows.anchor: قيل كانت دراهم زيوفا وقيل صوفا وسمنا. وقيل الصنوبر والحبة الخضراء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask Joseph to give them the full measure.
rows.anchor: فأتمم لنا الكيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal for charity may ask Joseph to return Benjamin, forgive and accept their poor payment, or give more than it is worth; scholars differ over whether charity is forbidden to all prophets or only to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: برد أخينا أو بالمسامحة وقبول المزجاة، أو بالزيادة على ما يساويها. واختلف في أن حرمة الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasadduq means granting favor generally, though customarily it means giving for God's reward; the Prophet called the shortened prayer a charity God granted and told people to accept it.
rows.anchor: تصدق الله بها عليكم فاقبلوا صدقته
